predecessors.name: Second Turkic Khaganate
predecessors.text: the western steppe between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya, the Oghuz country of the 700s

predecessors.name: Kangar Union
predecessors.text: the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes, taken from the Kangar union and the Pechenegs 'at the beginning of the 9th century'

successors.name: Kimek-Kipchak confederation
successors.text: the Oghuz lands, taken by the Kimeks and Kipchaks (Cumans); Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape of 1056 holds 1,424 of the 1,425 cells

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Khwarezm, from which the Seljuks drove Shah Malik out in 1043

ledger.x: 750: Oghuz Turks found the Oghuz Yabgu State between the Caspian and the Aral.
Early 9th century: the capital moves to Yangikent.
970: the Oghuz spread over the Turgay-Emba steppe.
985: Seljuk leaves the Oghuz and settles at Jend with his followers.
1034: yabghu Shah Malik fights the Seljuks in Khwarezm.
1041: Shah Malik conquers Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids.
1043: the Seljuks drive Shah Malik out of Khwarezm.
1043: the Khwarezm war ends with the Seljuks in possession.
1055: the Kimeks and Kipchaks take the Oghuz lands.

wars.name: Oghuz-Karluk struggle for Zhetysu
wars.outcome: After the Karluks overran the Turgesh in Zhetysu in 766 the Oghuz lost the struggle for leadership; many moved to the Karatau foothills and the Chu valley.

wars.name: Oghuz war on the Kangar union and the Pechenegs
wars.outcome: Allied with the Karluks and Kimeks, the Oghuz destroy the Kangar union and take the lower Syr Darya and Aral steppes, driving the Kangars and Pechenegs west (Oghuz Yabgu State: 'At the beginning of the 9th century'; Pecheneg page: the Oghuz, Karluks and…

wars.name: Oghuz-Rus' war on the Khazars
wars.outcome: 'In 965 the Oghuz State allied with Kievan Rus in a war against the Khazar Kaganate.'

wars.name: Oghuz-Rus' war on Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 985 the alliance with Kievan Rus defeated Volga Bulgaria.'

wars.name: Oghuz-Seljuk war for Khwarezm
wars.outcome: Shah Malik beats the Seljuks and Turkomans of Khwarezm (1034-1035), takes Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids (1041 or 1042) and is driven out by the Seljuks in 1043.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the page names rivers and seas, not lines.
